record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the paper and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports ablation and direction-addition results and names result artifacts for the refusal-direction experiments. The exact procedure cannot be verified from the README alone.
record.gate_note: Rows below use only results summarized in the README. The README also names other findings, figures, notebooks, and scripts; their contents were not available here. F20 is included because the README explicitly reports both internal-signature collapse and the absence of behavioural capture. Other-axis findings and artifacts without a reported result bearing on these versions are not rows.
record.test_reason: The README reports difference-in-means-style refusal-direction ablation (ASR 0→0.90) and addition (over-refusal +0.95) in Gemma-2-2b, and the same in Qwen2.5-3b. This is the original paper's intervention and measure pair. Procedure details (layers, prompt sets, judge) cannot be verified from the README alone.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that refusal has a shared necessary, ablatable single-direction core in Gemma-2-2b and Qwen2.5-3b, and that calibrated addition is sufficient in both. What stays model-specific is quantitative: dose window, effective dimension (1 vs 3) and EC50. Prompt injection collapses the internal signature without behavioural capture.
record.recipe_differences: The README reports residual-stream direction ablation and addition, but does not state enough procedural detail to verify the original extraction and intervention recipe. This is a research repository with summarized findings and result artifacts; the code and paper were not inspected.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says effective dimension and EC50 potency are model-specific and layer-dependent, and that the earlier fixed-64× addition asymmetry was a dose artifact.
record.problems: Evidence here is limited to README summaries; model, prompt-set, layer, judge, and evaluation details are mostly absent. General capability preservation is not reported. The README gives little uncertainty information, and some findings have no numerical outcomes in the provided text.
record.rows_left_out: No other README findings were included because they concern other axes or do not report outcomes bearing on these claim versions. The README's referenced paper, findings ledger, and figures were not available for inspection beyond their names in the file list.

untested.parts: Preservation of general abilities after ablation or addition is not reported.
Whether successful jailbreaks suppress the direction, and whether training against ablation adds robustness.
No affine or cone result is reported, though an affine module exists.
No transfer of a direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct is reported.
Abliterated checkpoints are mentioned as produced, but no refusal-removal result for a weight edit is given.

missing.what: F18/F19 effective-dimension sweep by layer and EC50 potency scaling, which give the layer dependence behind the V4 verdicts
F23 calibrated addition dose curves with numbers for Gemma and Qwen
Single-vs-affine dimensionality results (run_affine), not summarized in the README
F20 triangulation numbers, model, and attack setting

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is README summaries only. The work is a non-peer-reviewed repository mixing mechanistic work with analogy and metaphor tiers; only the mechanism tier is relevant here. No capability, uncertainty, or control details are given. The verdicts are weak until FINDINGS.md and the paper are read.

versions.untested_parts: Whether general abilities are largely preserved is not stated.
No released-model weight-edit result is reported.
Training against ablation and resulting robustness are not reported.
The README does not give details of affine or cone measurements.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision result is reported.
Transfer across languages, base-to-instruct models, and other model variants is not reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.
